ei.title: The Paradox of Renewable Energy Transition
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: Richard Heinberg, an American journalist, argues that in building the renewable energy infrastructure to stop global warming, we are actually involved in one of the greatest change projects in human history. In addition to solar panels and wind turbines, we have to build an alternative transport infrastructure, farming procedures and industrial processes. This transformation cannot happen without fossil fuels. For instance, production of concrete structures and steel elements require amounts of energy that is only possible to produce with fossil energy. Production of solar panels requires scarce and expensive minerals which must be excavated, again requiring the use of fossil fuels. Thus, the harder we push towards a renewable energy system, the faster we have to use fossil energy for the construction process. This is not only expensive, but also an undermining factor for our efforts to cut global emissions. Heinberg remarks that the cost of building this new energy infrastructure is seldom counted in transition proposals, which tend to focus just on energy supply requirements.

questions.passage: Richard Heinberg, an American journalist, argues that in building the renewable energy infrastructure ①<u>to stopping</u> global warming, we are actually involved in one of the greatest change projects in human history. In addition to solar panels and wind turbines, we have to build an alternative transport infrastructure, farming procedures and industrial processes. This transformation cannot ②<u>happen</u> without fossil fuels. For instance, production of concrete structures and steel elements require amounts of energy that is only possible to produce with fossil energy. Production of solar panels requires scarce and expensive minerals which must be ③<u>excavated</u>, again requiring the use of fossil fuels. Thus, the harder we push towards a renewable energy system, the faster we have to use fossil energy for the construction process. This is not only expensive, but also an undermining factor for our efforts to cut global emissions. Heinberg remarks that the cost of building this new energy infrastructure is seldom ④<u>counted</u> in transition proposals, which tend to focus just on energy supply requirements.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① to stopping → to stop: 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법 to부정사이므로 to 뒤에 동사원형 stop
det.analysis:
❌ ① to stopping → to stop: 'to stop global warming'은 '지구 온난화를 막기 위해'라는 목적의 부사적 용법 to부정사. to 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 to stopping은 오류 ←정답
✅ ② happen: 'This transformation cannot happen'에서 조동사 cannot+동사원형 — 적절
✅ ③ excavated: 'minerals which must be excavated'에서 조동사+be+과거분사 수동태 — 적절
✅ ④ counted: 'the cost ... is seldom counted'에서 비용은 계산되는 대상이므로 be+과거분사 수동태 — 적절
det.tip: 목적의 부사적 용법: to + 동사원형. to stop(O) / to stopping(X)

questions.passage: Richard Heinberg, an American journalist, argues that in building the renewable energy infrastructure to stop global warming, we are actually ①<u>involved</u> in one of the greatest change projects in human history. In addition to solar panels and wind turbines, we have to build an alternative transport infrastructure, farming procedures and industrial processes. This transformation cannot happen without fossil fuels. For instance, production of concrete structures and steel elements require amounts of energy ②<u>what is</u> only possible to produce with fossil energy. Production of solar panels requires scarce and expensive minerals which must be excavated, again requiring the use of fossil fuels. Thus, the harder we ③<u>push</u> towards a renewable energy system, the faster we have to use fossil energy for the construction process. This is not only expensive, but also an undermining factor for our efforts to cut global emissions. Heinberg remarks that the cost of building this new energy infrastructure is seldom counted in transition proposals, which tend to ④<u>focus</u> just on energy supply requirements.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② what is → that is: 선행사 energy가 있으므로 관계대명사 that(또는 which). what은 선행사를 포함하므로 사용 불가
det.analysis:
✅ ① involved: 'we are actually involved in'에서 수동 표현 — 적절
❌ ② what is → that is: 'amounts of energy that is only possible to produce'에서 선행사 energy가 있으므로 관계대명사 that(또는 which)이 와야 함. what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사라 선행사 뒤에 올 수 없어 오류 ←정답
✅ ③ push: 'we push towards'에서 주어 we에 맞는 동사원형 — 적절
✅ ④ focus: 'tend to focus'에서 to부정사의 동사원형 — 적절
det.tip: 선행사(energy) 있으면 that/which, 선행사 포함하면 what

questions.passage: Richard Heinberg, an American journalist, argues that in building the renewable energy infrastructure to ①<u>stop</u> global warming, we are actually involved in one of the greatest change projects in human history. In addition to solar panels and wind turbines, we have to build an alternative transport infrastructure, farming procedures and industrial processes. For instance, production of concrete structures and steel elements require amounts of energy that is only possible to produce with fossil energy. Production of solar panels requires scarce and expensive minerals which must be ③<u>excavated</u>, again ④<u>require</u> the use of fossil fuels. Thus, the harder we push towards a renewable energy system, the faster we have to use fossil energy for the construction process. This is not only expensive, but also an undermining factor for our efforts to cut global emissions. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ require → requiring: 'again requiring ...'은 분사구문이므로 현재분사 requiring이 와야 한다
det.analysis:
✅ ① stop: 'to stop global warming'에서 부사적 용법 to부정사 — 적절
✅ ② happen: 'cannot happen'에서 조동사+동사원형 — 적절
✅ ③ excavated: 'must be excavated'에서 수동태 과거분사 — 적절
❌ ④ require → requiring: 'again requiring the use of fossil fuels'는 앞 절에 이미 본동사(requires)가 있으므로 분사구문이 되어야 하며 현재분사 requiring이 적절. 동사원형 require는 접속사 없이 쓸 수 없어 오류 ←정답
det.tip: 접속사 없이 연결되는 동사 → 분사구문(V-ing): again requiring ~

questions.passage: Richard Heinberg, an American journalist, argues that in building the renewable energy infrastructure to stop global warming, we are actually involved in one of the ①<u>greatest</u> change projects in human history. In addition to solar panels and wind turbines, we have to build an ②<u>identical</u> transport infrastructure, farming procedures and industrial processes. This transformation cannot happen without fossil fuels. For instance, production of concrete structures and steel elements require amounts of energy that is only possible to produce with fossil energy. Production of solar panels requires scarce and expensive ③<u>minerals</u> which must be excavated, again requiring the use of fossil fuels. Thus, the harder we push towards a renewable energy system, the faster we have to use fossil energy for the construction process. This is not only expensive, but also an undermining factor for our efforts to cut global emissions. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② identical(동일한) → alternative(대체의): 기존과 다른 '대체' 교통 기반 시설을 지어야 한다는 맥락
det.analysis:
✅ ① greatest: 인류 역사상 가장 큰(greatest) 변화 프로젝트 — 적절
❌ ② identical → alternative: 원문은 '대체(alternative) 교통 기반 시설'. identical(동일한)로 바꾸면 기존과 동일한 시설을 짓는 것이 되어, 새로운 대체 시스템을 구축해야 한다는 맥락과 모순 ←정답
✅ ③ minerals: 희귀하고 값비싼 광물(minerals) — 적절
✅ ④ proposals: 전환 제안(proposals)은 공급 요구 사항에만 집중 — 적절
det.tip: alternative(대체의) ↔ identical(동일한)

questions.passage: Richard Heinberg, an American journalist, argues that in building the renewable energy infrastructure to stop global warming, we are actually involved in one of the greatest change projects in human history. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ supporting(지지하는) → undermining(훼손하는): 배기가스 감축 노력을 '훼손하는' 요인이라는 맥락
det.analysis:
✅ ① transport: 대체 교통(transport) 기반 시설 — 적절
✅ ② happen: 이 전환은 화석 연료 없이 일어날(happen) 수 없다 — 적절
❌ ③ supporting → undermining: 원문은 노력을 '훼손하는(undermining)' 요인. supporting(지지하는)으로 바꾸면 '배기가스 감축 노력을 지지하는 요인'이 되어, 비용이 들고 노력을 해친다는 부정적 맥락과 모순 ←정답
✅ ④ requirements: 에너지 공급 요구 사항(requirements) — 적절
det.tip: undermining(훼손하는) ↔ supporting(지지하는)

This transformation cannot happen without fossil fuels. For instance, production of concrete structures and steel elements require amounts of energy that __________. Production of solar panels requires scarce and expensive minerals which must be excavated, again requiring the use of fossil fuels. Thus, the harder we push towards a renewable energy system, the faster we have to use fossil energy for the construction process. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: is only possible to produce with fossil energy=화석 에너지로만 생산 가능한 — 콘크리트·강철 생산에 필요한 에너지의 특성
det.analysis:
✅ ① is only possible to produce with fossil energy(화석 에너지로만 생산 가능한): 바로 뒤 문장들이 재생 에너지 구축에 화석 연료가 필요하다는 논지를 펴므로, 콘크리트·강철 생산 에너지가 화석 에너지로만 가능하다는 내용이 적절 ←정답
❌ ② can easily be generated from sunlight alone(햇빛만으로 쉽게 생성되는): 화석 연료 의존이라는 글의 논지와 반대
❌ ③ requires no external power source(외부 전원이 전혀 필요 없는): 에너지가 많이 필요하다는 맥락과 반대
❌ ④ is freely available almost everywhere(거의 모든 곳에서 자유롭게 이용 가능한): 희소성·비용 강조와 모순
det.tip: concrete structures and steel elements require amounts of energy that __________ → 화석 에너지로만 생산 가능

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: one of the greatest change projects in human history=인류 역사상 가장 큰 변화 프로젝트 중 하나 — 재생 에너지 기반 시설 구축의 규모

questions.passage: Richard Heinberg, an American journalist, argues that in building the renewable energy infrastructure to stop global warming, we are actually involved in one of the greatest change projects in human history. This transformation cannot happen without fossil fuels. For instance, production of concrete structures and steel elements require amounts of energy that is only possible to produce with fossil energy. Production of solar panels requires scarce and expensive minerals which must be excavated, again requiring the use of fossil fuels. Thus, the harder we push towards a renewable energy system, the faster we have to use fossil energy for the construction process. This is not only expensive, but also an undermining factor for our efforts to cut global emissions. Heinberg remarks that the cost of building this new energy infrastructure is seldom counted in transition proposals, which tend to focus just on energy supply requirements.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 본문 S2와 일치
det.analysis:
❌ ① 즉시 완전히 없앤다: 본문은 건설 과정에 화석 에너지를 더 써야 한다고 서술 — 불일치
❌ ② 흔하고 저렴한 광물: 본문 'scarce and expensive minerals'(희귀하고 값비싼) — 불일치
✅ ③ 대체 시스템 구축 수반: 본문 S2 'we have to build an alternative transport infrastructure, farming procedures and industrial processes'와 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ 항상 정확히 계산: 본문 'seldom counted'(거의 계산되지 않는) — 불일치
det.tip: In addition to A, we have to build B, C and D = A 외에 B·C·D도 구축해야 한다

ch: 재생 에너지 전환은 화석 연료 사용을 즉시 완전히 없앤다.
태양광 패널은 흔하고 저렴한 광물만으로 만들어진다.
재생 에너지 기반 시설 구축은 대체 교통·농업·산업 시스템 구축을 수반한다.
Heinberg는 전환 비용이 제안에서 항상 정확히 계산된다고 본다.
